tier_reason: The README Benchmark Results tables match the record: 489.5 vs 851.6 us (1.7x) on point queries, 7.7 vs 25.0 MB memory, and 120.5 vs 174.3 us on range scans against BTreeSet. The Criterion harness is public (benches/pgm_bench.rs) and Cargo.toml sets [profile.bench] lto=true, codegen-units=1, with opt-level=3 inherited from release. The CPU is named (Apple M1 Pro), but no rustc version is given, so under the convention earlier batches used for Rust this is first-party C, not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc (version not stated); Cargo [profile.bench] lto=true, codegen-units=1 (opt-level=3 inherited from [profile.release]); Criterion harness benches/pgm_bench.rs
corrections.caveats: First-party Criterion micro-benchmark on a single machine (Apple M1 Pro) with no rustc version stated, not independently reproduced. The point-query workload is 10K queries at a 50% hit ratio over 1M random u64 keys. In the same table, a plain binary search over the sorted Vec (266.8 us) and HashMap (68.2 us) both beat every PGM variant (489.5 us at best), so the win is specific to BTreeSet/BTreeMap and to memory footprint. This is a from-scratch Rust reimplementation of the PGM-index idea, not a fork of the canonical gvinciguerra/PGM-index (already catalogued).

notes: Metadata checks out: MIT, not a fork, not archived, 107 stars, last commit 2026-07-28. The default branch is main, so blob/master only redirects and the URL was changed to main. Worth noting when enriching: the README's own table shows binary search on a sorted array beating PGM at this size.

tier_reason: This is a peer-reviewed paper (PVLDB 18(9):2886-2898, 2025) whose public artifact is github.com/qyliu-hkust/bench_search (exp_pgm/main.cpp). It shows up to 2.31x over the original PGM-Index, and the CPUs and compilers are stated (i7-13700K and EPYC 7413 with g++ 11.4; Apple M3 with clang++ 15), so it would ordinarily be B. It is capped at C because the paper states no optimization flags, and the artifact's only documented builds pass no -O flag: the README's 'g++ main.cpp -std=c++17 -I. -o main -fopenmp' and exp_rmi/Makefile_all. That means both the PGM baseline and PGM++ are built at the -O0 default.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Up to 2.31x faster lookups than the original PGM-Index and up to 1.56x faster than state-of-the-art learned indexes (CDFShop-optimized RMI) at comparable space cost (abstract). In the paper body, PGM++ beats PGM by 1.2x-2.2x at the same index size on Uniform query workloads, and RMI still beats PGM++ on the synthetic normal dataset.
corrections.workload: Lookup queries on 4 SOSD real datasets (fb and wiki at 200M uint64 keys; books and osm at 800M) plus 3 synthetic ones (uniform, normal, lognormal). PGM++ (a mixture of internal search strategies with epsilon tuned by a cost model) is compared with the original PGM-Index and CDFShop-optimized RMI at comparable index size on three platforms. B+-tree and other non-learned baselines are deliberately excluded.
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i7-13700K (Ubuntu 20.04, 32/64 GB DDR4); 2x AMD EPYC 7413 (CentOS 9.4, 1 TB DDR4); Apple M3 MacBook Air (macOS 14.4.1, 16 GB)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: g++ 11.4 on the two x86 platforms and clang++ 15 on ARM (per paper); optimization flags are not stated in the paper. The artifact's documented builds pass no -O flag: README 'g++ main.cpp -std=c++17 -I. -o main -fopenmp' and exp_rmi/Makefile_all.
corrections.is_fork_of: derived from gvinciguerra/PGM-index (vendored, modified pgm_index.h / piecewise_linear_model.h; not a GitHub fork)
corrections.stars_or_usage: Artifact repo qyliu-hkust/bench_search: 6 stars; paper in PVLDB 18(9):2886-2898 (2025), doi:10.14778/3746405.3746415
corrections.caveats: Research artifact, not a library: the code is at github.com/qyliu-hkust/bench_search (exp_pgm/), which is linked from the paper's PVLDB Artifact Availability box, so the record's 'no code released' is wrong. The repo has no LICENSE. Its vendored PGM-index headers keep their Apache-2.0 notices, but the PGM++-specific files (search_algo.h, main.cpp, utils.h) are unlicensed. Optimization flags are unstated, and the documented build commands use the -O0 default for both PGM and PGM++. There is no B+-tree or std baseline, only learned indexes. The paper is by Qiyu Liu et al. (Southwest University / HKUST), not the PGM-index authors. gvinciguerra/Learned-indexes-effectiveness belongs to a different, earlier paper (Ferragina, Lillis, Vinciguerra, ICML 2020).

tier_reason: The 2026-08-26 run JSON has libzmq@4.3.5 and monocoque@0.4.1 records that match the claim: IPC 1024B p50 13.79 vs 42.16 us and p99 16.80 vs 47.49 us, with 2.75x-3.12x at 64/1024/16384B. The code is public in vorjdux/zmq-arena: targets/monocoque_target/src/main.rs, targets/libzmq_cpp_target/src/main.cpp and the orchestrator. The build flags are pinned: rustc 1.96.0 with opt-level=3, lto, codegen-units=1 and target-cpu=x86-64-v3; the C++ wrapper uses -O3 -flto -march=x86-64-v3 with Ubuntu 24.04 g++. The CPU (i5-13400) is recorded, so A holds.

corrections.claimed_speedup: REQ/REP p50 latency 2.75x-3.12x lower than libzmq 4.3.5 across IPC and TCP at 64B/1024B/16384B payloads. Example: IPC 1024B, monocoque 13.79us vs libzmq 42.16us at p50 and 16.80us vs 47.49us at p99. Across all six payloads (16B-16KiB) the compio backend is 2.69x-3.12x. The tokio backend reaches about 4.3x at IPC 16B-1KiB (9.36-9.70us vs 40.17-42.16us p50). The same run shows about 2.0x-4.7x higher single-pair throughput than libzmq (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: monocoque target: rustc 1.96.0 (rust-toolchain.toml plus Dockerfile), [profile.release] opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3'. libzmq target: Ubuntu 24.04 build-essential g++, CMake Release with '-O3 -flto -march=x86-64-v3' for the wrapper, linked against the Ubuntu libzmq5 4.3.5 distro package.
corrections.workload: REQ/REP round trip over TCP (per-run network namespace with private loopback) and IPC (Unix domain socket), payload sizes 16B-16KiB, one socket pair per cell. libzmq 4.3.5 (Ubuntu 24.04 package, 1 I/O thread) is compared with monocoque 0.4.1 (default compio/io_uring backend, plus tokio and smol backends). Each cell runs 5-11 replicates with MAD outlier rejection inside a cgroup v2 leaf (cpuset 0-3, 256 MiB memory cap). Each implementation is built in a pinned Docker image and then exec'd directly on bare metal (chroot plus network namespace, no container runtime) under zmq-arena's harness.
corrections.caveats: The harness (vorjdux/zmq-arena, 1 star, Apache-2.0) is written by monocoque's own author, and no independent third party has reproduced the result. Only two runs are published (2026-08-21 and 2026-08-26), both on a single machine (i5-13400, turbo off). The libzmq baseline is Ubuntu's distro-built libzmq5, not built with the harness flags. The same run also covers throughput, pub/sub (32 subscribers) and fan-in/fan-out (4 peers), where monocoque mostly leads too; the one loss is fan-in at 16B, 0.94x. One cell, compio IPC 64B, is flagged unstable. The run tested 0.4.1; crates.io now has monocoque-rs 0.4.2. The repo is small (46 stars; the crate has 312 downloads).

notes: The numbers match the run JSON exactly. The record's caveat 'single socket pair, no fan-out or multi-peer contention' was wrong, since the run includes pub/sub and fan-in/fan-out cells. Metadata checks out: MIT, not a fork, 46 stars, last commit 2026-09-22.
